name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa; Sudan and Yemen among worst affected
state: WHO said around 10 Nov that more than 3,000 people have died of cholera in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa, with Sudan, South Sudan, DR Congo, Nigeria and Yemen among high-burden countries (SCMP). WHO reported a cholera surge in Yemen as conflict intensified (Al Jazeera, 13 Oct). Searches on 17 Nov found no sign of the toll easing, so high mortality in conflict-affected countries keeps the Alert.
for_you: Risk to most travellers is low. Anyone visiting affected areas should follow FCDO travel advice and NHS Fit for Travel guidance on safe water, food hygiene and cholera vaccination.
rubric_hit: Alert: large cholera outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones (Sudan, Yemen); 3,000+ deaths in 2026 (WHO)

sources.title: Over 3,000 already dead from cholera this year, says WHO
Cholera cases surge in Yemen as conflict intensifies, WHO says

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
